answer: An agent economy resists sybils with work watermarking: every output an identity produces carries a hidden mark bound to its key, like a river carrying a distinct mineral trace from its source. Peers compare marks across identities, and when the same mark lineage appears under many names, the whole cluster is slashed at its zenith of earnings. A farm's thousand fakes must therefore produce a thousand genuinely different work streams, paying full creation cost per fake, while one honest agent watermarks its own work once — and the delta between copying and creating becomes the attacker's bill.
